title: Weekly links October 9: rich data on jobs for economists, new work on firms and trade, the price women pay for violent men, and more…
gist: A World Bank Development Impact link roundup covering PhD economist job-market outcomes, the education and labor cost to Indian women of anticipated harassment, Lant Pritchett's argument that narrow targeting has eroded political support for foreign aid, well-timed loans to Nepali migrant families raising rice harvests 12%, and Vietnamese firms dodging labor-law thresholds via unpaid labor.

insights.claim: Of 784 economics PhD graduates of the class of 2026 tracked in a new dataset, 36% took tenure-track jobs, 25% postdoctoral or other academic positions, and 22% private-sector jobs.
insights.so_what: Over a fifth of new economics PhDs flow to private-sector employers, a talent pipeline for finance and tech research teams.
insights.quote: Of the 784 graduates of the class of 2026 listed so far, 36% took tenure-track positions, 25% postdoctoral or other academic positions, and 22% private-sector jobs.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: A public database covering almost 15,000 economics PhD graduates from 80 programs (1990-2026) lets users see placement by department, employer and year, including names of private-sector hires.
insights.so_what: Useful hiring-intelligence tool for mapping which firms recruit economists and from where.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Research on India estimates that the mere anticipation of harassment imposes a cost equivalent to 17 percent on women's college choices, even for women who are never harassed or assaulted.
insights.so_what: Safety, not admissions meritocracy, is a binding constraint on female human-capital accumulation in India.
insights.quote: That estimate—17 percent—isn't the cost to women who are harassed or assaulted. It's the cost of anticipating harassment and planning one's education around it
insights.locator: On the CGD blog, Eeshani Kandpal
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: In Delhi and Bengaluru, roughly 70 percent of women who were not students said fear of harassment affected whether they worked at all.
insights.so_what: Public safety is a direct lever on India's notoriously low female labor-force participation and thus growth potential.
insights.quote: roughly 70 percent of women who weren't students said fear of harassment mattered for whether they worked at all.
insights.locator: On the CGD blog, Eeshani Kandpal
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Lant Pritchett argues global foreign-aid cuts reflect aid's post-1990 narrowing from broad systemic country transformation ('getting to Denmark') to targeted mitigation of specific harms like health, nutrition, education and credit access.
insights.so_what: Explains why donor budgets are shrinking and suggests aid that survives will be repackaged around growth and strategic interest.
insights.quote: This shifted development assistance from the broad, systemic transformation of countries — what Fukuyama calls “getting to Denmark” — to projects focused on the targeted
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: By concentrating on the poorest, most struggling countries, aid loses soft-power value because those are not the countries where donors have their strongest foreign-policy interests.
insights.so_what: Expect aid reallocation toward geopolitically strategic middle-income countries, hurting the poorest recipients.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Narrowly targeted social benefit programs, like narrowly targeted aid, may command less political support than programs with broader eligibility.
insights.so_what: Universal-style programs are more politically durable, relevant for forecasting fiscal policy persistence.
insights.quote: Likewise, narrowly targeted benefits programs may have less political support than those with broader eligibility.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: In Nepal, migrant workers could not remit wages electronically across the border, so money arrived only at harvest rather than in the lean season when it was most valuable to families.
insights.so_what: Shows large untapped value in cross-border digital remittance rails for frontier markets.
insights.quote: Because technology to remit wages electronically across the border did not exist, most workers only brought money back home when they returned for the harvest season.
insights.locator: On Yale’s SOM website, Mushfiq Mobarak
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Small loans timed to migrants' work-travel cadence raised Nepali families' nitrogen fertilizer investment by 17%, household farm labor by 3.4-3.6 hours weekly, and rice harvests by 12%.
insights.so_what: Well-designed seasonal microcredit has measurable agricultural productivity returns, supporting agri-fintech business models.
insights.quote: among families that received the loan, investment in nitrogen fertilizer increased by 17% and weekly labor on household farms increased by 3.4-3.6 hours
insights.locator: On Yale’s SOM website, Mushfiq Mobarak
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: When Vietnam raised the cost of non-compliance with labor laws that apply at 10 or more paid workers, firms responded by using more unpaid labor such as family workers and only partially formalizing.
insights.so_what: Size-threshold regulations create bunching and informality, limiting the formal-sector gains enforcement aims for.
insights.quote: Firms increased their use of unpaid labor such as family workers, and partially rather than fully formalized.
insights.locator: On the Econ that Matters blog
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Research from a firms, trade and development conference shows policies affect not only their targeted outcomes but work through many other adjustment margins, and gains can diverge between firm owners and workers.
insights.so_what: Policy-impact analysis should anticipate second-order adjustments and distributional splits between capital and labor.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
